fatal_errors: The proposed FCC metals are unrelated to the target single-BCC-phase NbMoTaW and NbMoTaWRe refractory high-entropy-alloy films.
It omits the central intervention: Re addition and comparison before and after 120 keV He2+ implantation.
It replaces the target defect-sink and helium-bubble suppression mechanism with a generic slip-system argument.
It provides no evidence supporting its material recommendation.

The blanket claim that FCC metals are more ductile because they have more slip systems is oversimplified; ductility also depends strongly on dislocation mobility, temperature, chemistry, microstructure, and deformation mode.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses ductility only in a broad sense and does not reconstruct the material system, irradiation treatment, comparison baseline, mechanism, or outcomes of the target study. The target supports Re-containing BCC NbMoTaWRe films for improved resistance to irradiation-induced hardening and grain-boundary embrittlement, attributed to refined grains, excess free volume, amorphous boundary regions, and enhanced defect annihilation. The proposed tensile-test experiment is measurable but poorly controlled because comparing unrelated FCC and BCC metals confounds crystal structure with composition and microstructure.
